accepted_units.title: From raw representations to closed orbits and Jordan equivalence
accepted_units.why_material: Makes explicit what quotienting forgets: raw isomorphism classes are replaced by closed-orbit representatives, with nonclosed orbits mapped to their semisimplifications.

accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires a smooth projective family, local systems of schemes, monodromy/outer actions, and framed versus coarse spaces.
accepted_units.title: Relative Betti moduli as locally constant families with descent
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how a fiberwise representation construction becomes a local system of schemes and why framed spaces retain basepoint/path choices while coarse quotients can lose them.

accepted_units.title: Higgs moduli, associated graded objects, and scaling fixed points
accepted_units.why_material: Connects Jordan equivalence to associated gradeds, identifies closed points with polystable/harmonic objects, and uses scaling of the Higgs field to expose graded fixed-point structure.

accepted_units.context_note: This is an alternative construction of the same functor, not a claim that every formula survived OCR; exact sheaf/module notation needs checking.

accepted_units.title: Re-encoding Higgs data as spectral sheaves
accepted_units.why_material: Provides a reusable representation move: algebraic operator data become geometric support data, while flatness, purity, torsion-freeness, and stability are tracked across the encoding.

accepted_units.context_note: The spectral-curve example is application context; the accepted content is the support/properness/degeneration mechanism. Displayed characteristic-polynomial formulas are OCR-fragile.

accepted_units.title: Proper invariants turn scaling into controlled degeneration
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how an invariant map and properness prevent escape at infinity and force a scaling orbit to acquire a fixed-point limit; this is a general compactness-through-invariants pattern.

accepted_units.context_note: Automatic local freeness and Chern-class vanishing are cited results, not established from scratch here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on differential-operator module machinery from Part I and distinguishes framed de Rham spaces from their basepoint-independent coarse quotient.
accepted_units.title: Integrability as a moduli condition with framed/coarse separation
accepted_units.why_material: Packages flatness as zero curvature and explains why changing a basepoint is transparent analytically for framed objects but algebraically uncertain, whereas the coarse quotient is intrinsic.

accepted_units.context_note: The local analytic lemma is proof-heavy and some formulas are corrupted; its role is to justify relative horizontal sections over possibly nonreduced bases.

accepted_units.title: Relative Riemann-Hilbert as equality of represented analytic functors
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the framed Betti/de Rham analytic isomorphism by showing that both spaces represent the same analytic family problem, then descends it to coarse moduli.

accepted_units.context_note: Compactness and regularity arguments use Uhlenbeck, elliptic estimates, and the harmonic-bundle results of the cited companion paper; exact analytic hypotheses should not be weakened.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires existence/uniqueness of harmonic metrics for semisimple flat bundles and polystable zero-Chern Higgs bundles, plus weak compactness.
accepted_units.title: Harmonic representatives produce a homeomorphism, not an analytic isomorphism
accepted_units.why_material: Uses a common harmonic representative and compact quotient topology to compare de Rham and Dolbeault moduli while carefully limiting the result to a topological homeomorphism.

accepted_units.context_note: The displayed elliptic-curve matrices are especially OCR-damaged, but the limiting-dependence conclusion and its scope are clear.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses an explicit degenerating family of framed Higgs bundles and its associated flat connections.
accepted_units.title: A counterexample separates coarse continuity from framed continuity
accepted_units.why_material: Demonstrates that a categorical bijection can fail to be continuous before quotienting even when the stable-locus comparison and coarse moduli homeomorphism behave well.

accepted_units.context_note: The formal Taylor expansions and differential equations are OCR-sensitive; the robust content is the equivalence between flat infinitesimal transport and integrability.

accepted_units.title: Integrable connection as coherent infinitesimal transport
accepted_units.why_material: Reframes a differential condition as transport along infinitesimally close points; the cocycle becomes precisely the compatibility whose infinitesimal obstruction is curvature.

accepted_units.context_note: Terminology is acknowledged by the source as potentially nonstandard; use the definitions here rather than importing modern variants silently.

accepted_units.why_material: Shows that compatible data on all infinitesimal thickenings can be reconstructed from formal diagonal transport and are invariant under replacing a scheme by a nilpotent closed subscheme.

accepted_units.context_note: Representability is transferred from functors to schemes; the final comparison with Betti local constancy is theorem-level and depends on the previous analytic equivalence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires crystals of moduli functors, (co)representability, stratifications, and the Betti/de Rham analytic identification.
accepted_units.title: Gauss-Manin connection from crystalline functoriality
accepted_units.why_material: Builds a nonabelian Gauss-Manin connection by first making the moduli problem crystalline, then transporting that stratification to the representing scheme and matching it with Betti local constancy.

accepted_units.title: Principal objects reconstructed from their associated representations
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces one principal bundle by a coherent tensor-compatible family of associated bundles and supplies a converse reconstruction, exposing which categorical structure preserves the original object.

accepted_units.title: Invariant subobjects detect reduction of structure group
accepted_units.why_material: Characterizes containment of monodromy in a subgroup by the existence of compatible sub-Higgs bundles across representations, converting a group-theoretic condition into functorial linear data.

accepted_units.context_note: The quotient construction relies on GIT from Part I and standard results on reductive groups/parabolics; the one-parameter degeneration proof is source-specific evidence for the general closed-orbit criterion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires reductive G, a faithful linear representation, principal Higgs representation spaces, and universal categorical quotients.
accepted_units.title: Closed principal-bundle orbits are exactly reductive monodromy
accepted_units.why_material: Extends the framed/coarse distinction to principal groups and identifies closed orbits through complete reducibility; nonreductive monodromy is exposed by a one-parameter degeneration to a smaller limit group.

accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses stratified principal bundles, tensor functors with integrable connection, subgroup monodromy conditions, and Riemann-Hilbert.
accepted_units.title: Principal de Rham moduli and functorial Betti comparison
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that the tensor/subobject machinery survives replacement of Higgs fields by flat connections and that the analytic Betti comparison respects group homomorphisms, monodromy closure, and Gauss-Manin transport.

accepted_units.context_note: The maximal-compact argument and harmonic metric decompositions are technically dense; exact displayed formulas and group symbols require page verification.

accepted_units.why_material: Explains why choosing harmonic representatives converts a noncompact complex-group quotient into a proper quotient by a maximal compact group and makes the de Rham/Dolbeault correspondence topological.

accepted_units.why_material: Shows how eliminating inessential chain-level data yields a cohomological obstruction cone, then transfers its formal local structure through quotienting to obtain étale isosingularity across realizations.

accepted_units.why_material: Provides a general dynamical criterion: if every fixed point outside one connected core is reached as a nontrivial scaling limit, no separate connected component can survive; normality then upgrades connectedness to irreducibility.
